title: My biography

Stage 1 · Intro

My biography

Talk about the past with was and were — where you were, when, and how it was.

Stage 5 · Grammar

Grammar

was and were — the past of be.
Track 6.2 — was/were questions and short answersOriginal coursebook recording
Show transcript
1 — Was there a bobsleigh team at the Olympics? — Yes, there was. 2 — Was it easy for them to practise? — No, it wasn't. 3 — Were there bobsleighs for them to use? — No, there weren't. 4 — Were they popular? — Yes, they were.
1Was there a bobsleigh team at the Olympics?
2Was it easy for them to practise?
3Were there bobsleighs for them to use?
4Were they popular?
Why

Short answers repeat was / were: Yes, there was · No, it wasn't · No, there weren't · Yes, they were.

1Was there a bobsleigh team at the Olympics?
2Was it easy for them to practise?
3Were they popular?
Why

Short answers repeat was / were: Yes, there was · No, it wasn't · Yes, they were.

1Was there a bobsleigh team at the Olympics?
2Was it easy for them to practise?
3Were they popular?
Why

Short answers repeat was / were: Yes, there was · No, it wasn't · Yes, they were.

In other words
“I was born in 2001.”
“You were at school with me.”
“She was my first teacher.”
“They were on holiday last week.”
Notice

Notice: am / is → ? in the past. are → ? Look at the examples.

PersonPositiveNegativeQuestionShort answer
I / he / she / itI was at home.She wasn't happy.Was he there?Yes, he was. / No, he wasn't.
you / we / theyThey were at school.We weren't late.Were you there?Yes, I was. / No, they weren't.
In other words
was / were is the past of be: I am → I was; they are → they were.
Negative: wasn't = was not · weren't = were not.
Question: put was/were first — “Was she at home?”, “Where were you?”
Short answers repeat was/were: “Yes, I was.” — never “Yes, I was at home yesterday at eight o'clock.”
The past of ordinary verbs (worked, went) comes in Lessons 2–3.
Notice

Notice: am / is → ? in the past. are → ? Tell your partner.

In other words
was / were is the past of be: I am → I was; they are → they were.
Negative: wasn't · weren't. Question: was/were first — “Where were you?”
Short answers repeat was/were: “Yes, I was.”
Notice

Notice: am / is → ? in the past. are → ? Tell your teacher.

In other words
was / were is the past of be: I am → I was; they are → they were.
Negative: wasn't · weren't. Question: was/were first — “Where were you?”
Short answers repeat was/were: “Yes, I was.”
Stage 6 · Practice

Practice

Part 1 — was or were?
1I ___ born in 1999.
2My parents ___ teachers.
3The weather ___ terrible yesterday.
4You ___ at my school, right?
5There ___ no internet in 1980.
6We ___ on holiday last week.
Why

I / he / she / it / there → was. You / we / they → were.

1❌ “She were at home last night.”
2❌ “They wasn't happy.”
3❌ “Where you were yesterday?”
4❌ “Was they at university?”
Why

she was · they weren't · questions: Where were you…? / Were they…?

1Today I ___ a teacher.
2In 2015 I ___ a student.
3They ___ in Astana now.
4They ___ in London last year.
Why

now / today → am / is / are. last year / in 2015 → was / were.

1My grandfather ___ a pilot.
2The children ___ at school.
3There ___ forty people at the party.
4It ___ cold last night.
Why

he / she / it / there(+one) → was. you / we / they / there(+many) → were.

1❌ “We was on holiday in July.”
2❌ “He weren't at work yesterday.”
3❌ “When you were born?”
Why

we were · he wasn't · questions: When were you born?

1Today we ___ in class.
2Last summer we ___ at the seaside.
3She ___ a doctor now.
4She ___ a student five years ago.
Why

now / today → am / is / are. ago / last summer → was / were.

1My grandfather ___ a pilot.
2The children ___ at school.
3There ___ forty people at the party.
4It ___ cold last night.
Why

he / she / it / there(+one) → was. you / we / they / there(+many) → were.

1❌ “We was on holiday in July.”
2❌ “He weren't at work yesterday.”
3❌ “When you were born?”
Why

we were · he wasn't · questions: When were you born?

1Today we ___ in class.
2Last summer we ___ at the seaside.
3She ___ a doctor now.
4She ___ a student five years ago.
Why

now / today → am / is / are. ago / last summer → was / were.

Stage 7 · Firsts

Firsts

Six world firsts.

Listen. Choose the date you hear.

Track 6.3 — world firsts and their datesOriginal coursebook recording
Show transcript
1 — The first football World Cup was in the last century, in 1930. 2 — The first Olympic Games were about 2,800 years ago, in 776 BCE. 3 — The first dishwasher was in the 19th century. 4 — The first Sony Walkman was in 1979. 5 — The first talking film was in 1927. 6 — The first Oscars ceremony was in 1929.
1The first football World Cup was in…
2The first Olympic Games were about…
3The first Sony Walkman was in…
4The first talking film was in…
Why

World Cup — 1930 · Olympic Games — about 2,800 years ago · Walkman — 1979 · talking film — 1927.

A famous true story from the 1988 Winter Olympics.

Listen once. Then choose True or False.

Track 6.1 — the Jamaican bobsleigh teamOriginal coursebook recording
Show transcript
People were surprised to see a bobsleigh team from Jamaica at the 1988 Winter Olympics in Canada. It wasn't very easy for the team to practise in Jamaica before the Olympics because there was no ice and there were no bobsleighs for them to use. They weren't successful in their races, but they were very popular with the people watching because they tried so hard. There was a film telling their story in 1993 called Cool Runnings and it was a huge success, making $150,000,000 around the world.
1The team was from Jamaica.
2It was easy to practise in Jamaica.
3They were successful in their races.
4They were very popular.
Why

There was no ice in Jamaica, so practice wasn't easy. They weren't successful, but they were popular because they tried so hard.

Stage 8 · Listen

Listen

Amina's storyRead aloud by your device
Show transcript
I was born in Almaty in 1998. My home town is big and noisy, but our street was always quiet. My first school was small, and my grandmother was my first teacher — she was a maths teacher. My first job was in a café. It was hard work, but the people were friendly.
Daniyar's storyRead aloud by your device
Show transcript
I was born in 2001, in a small town near Astana. We were five children at home, so our flat was never quiet! In 2019 I was a student at university. My first job was in a bank. It wasn't very interesting, but my colleagues were kind.
Lena's storyRead aloud by your device
Show transcript
I was born in Moscow. When I was a child, we were often at my grandparents' house in the country. The summers there were perfect. My first job was in a bookshop. The salary wasn't big — but the books were free!
Three people talk about their lives.

Play each one. Then choose True or False.

1Amina's grandmother was her first teacher.
2Amina's first job was in a bank.
3Daniyar's family was small.
4Daniyar's colleagues at the bank were kind.
5Lena's summers in the country were perfect.
6Lena's salary at the bookshop was big.
Why

Amina's first job was in a café. Daniyar's family was big — five children. Lena's salary wasn't big, but the books were free.

Three people talk about their lives.

Play each one. Then answer the questions.

1Who was born in Almaty?
2Whose first job was in a bank?
3Where was Lena when she was a child?
4Whose first teacher was her grandmother?
Why

Amina — Almaty, her grandmother was her first teacher. Daniyar — the bank. Lena — summers at her grandparents' house.

Stage 9 · Write

Write

Write the short version of your life.

5–6 sentences with was / were.

Useful language
  • I was born in…
  • My home town is…
  • My first school was…
  • When I was a child…
  • My first job was…
  • It was…
Interview your partner about their life.

Make notes. Then tell another pair one interesting thing.

Useful language
  • Where were you born?
  • How was it?
  • Who was your…?
  • I was born in…
  • It was great / terrible
  • My first job was…
Interview your teacher about their life.

Make notes. Then tell your teacher one interesting thing.

Useful language
  • Where were you born?
  • How was it?
  • Who was your…?
  • I was born in…
  • It was great / terrible
  • My first job was…
In other words
Step 1 — ask your partner: Where were you born? Where was your first school? How was it? Who was your first teacher? What was your first job?
Step 2 — swap roles.
Step 3 — tell another pair one interesting thing: “Her first job was in a café.”
In other words
Step 1 — ask your teacher: Where were you born? Where was your first school? How was it? Who was your first teacher? What was your first job?
Step 2 — swap roles.
Step 3 — tell your teacher one interesting thing: “Her first job was in a café.”
Stage 10 · Type it

Type it

Now produce it — type, don’t tap.

Spelling counts. Type the answers, then check.

1I ___ at home yesterday. (be)
2They ___ at school last week. (be)
3Where ___ you born?
Why

was (I/he/she/it) \u00b7 were (you/we/they) \u00b7 negative: wasn't/weren't \u00b7 question: Was he\u2026?

1She were a doctor.
2You was late yesterday.
3I borned in 2001.
Why

was (I/he/she/it) \u00b7 were (you/we/they) \u00b7 negative: wasn't/weren't \u00b7 question: Was he\u2026?

1Make it negative: I was at work.
2Make a question: He was happy.
3Change to THEY: She was tired.
Why

was (I/he/she/it) \u00b7 were (you/we/they) \u00b7 negative: wasn't/weren't \u00b7 question: Was he\u2026?
